name: LANSQUENET
description: Lansquenet (from the French spelling of German 'Landsknecht' meaning 'servant of the land') is one of the oldest recorded banking card games, dating to at least 1542. It is an extremely simple gambling game where players bet on whether a player card or the dealer's card will appear first from the deck. Purely a game of chance with no skill involved, it was notorious in European military camps and royal courts for its rapid betting and potential for large losses.

content.text: Lansquenet (from the French spelling of German 'Landsknecht' meaning 'servant of the land') is one of the oldest recorded banking card games, dating to at least 1542. It is an extremely simple gambling game where players bet on whether a player card or the dealer's card will appear first from the deck. Purely a game of chance with no skill involved, it was notorious in European military camps and royal courts for its rapid betting and potential for large losses.

Developed by the Landsknechts, the colorful and violent mercenary pikemen of the Holy Roman Empire, around 1480-1500. The game was first documented in the 1542 edition of Rabelais' Gargantua and Pantagruel.
One Banker (Dealer) and any number of bettors. Minimum 2 players total.
Standard 52-card deck. Multiple decks (2-4) are often shuffled together to reduce ties.
Cards and a flat surface. A 'shoe' or dealing box is traditionally used.
The banker shuffles the deck(s) and places them in a shoe or pile. No cards are dealt to players initially.

items.text: Baccara: A more complex descendant of banking games with more elaborate rules.
Pharo: 19th-century American gambling staple with similar logic but more complex betting options.
Red Dog: Simplified modern version of the banking game concept.
Skin: English variant with slightly different rules for bank rotation.
